newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: FORECAST - NUTRICIA 1996 NET SEEN UP OVER 50 PCT.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - NUTRICIA 1996 NET SEEN UP OVER 50 PCT.

text.p: Dutch food group Nutricia's 1996 net profits are expected to have soared by over 50 percent, with impetus still coming from the success of its purchase of baby food group Milupa, analysts said on Tuesday.
They expect the group to post 1996 net profits from ordinary operations of between 220 and 237 million guilders on Thursday, with a consensus of 230 million, versus 152 million in 1995.
In August, Nutricia reported a 51 percent rise in first half net profit to 107 million guilders and said the impressive pace of growth was set to continue through the year.

"There are no big surprises expected, because of their own indications at the half year," said Bank Bangert Pontier analyst John Ebbing. "It is mainly the same story of growth on Milupa, but Nutricia stays a Buy."
Bangert sees profits of 237 million guilders, at the upper end of the range of forecasts.

Nutricia bought German baby food maker Milupa for 920 million guilders in August 1995. The financial benefits of the acquisition have fed through faster than envisaged as the company has been quickly integrated.

Bank Labouchere analyst John David Roeg said he was also sticking to his Buy recommendation for the group, with growth prospects good for its core product groups. Labouchere forecasts profits of 229 million guilders.
Nutricia is European market leader in infant milk formula, baby cereals and enteral clinical nutrition (ECN).
Enteral clinical food is used for patients who cannot or are unwilling to eat. Products include tube feeds and liquid meals.
Roeg sees demand growing strongly for ECN products, partly due to the ageing population in Europe, with sales growth of around 15 percent per year expected in coming years.

Baby meals and cereals are also expected to show healthy sales growth, with Nutricia's key milk formula business insulated from falling birthrates in Europe by the company's clout in emerging markets in Eastern Europe and Asia.
The expected sparkling results have been slightly overshadowed by the latest in a series of Salmonella scares.
Milupa said last Thursday it was withdrawing some baby formula in France after discovering that raw materials from an outside supplier had been tainted with the toxic bacteria.

Nutricia's shares fell 17.80 guilders, or 6.21 percent, that day, compared to a 3.36 percent dip in the AEX index, though the company said that, given the limited scale of the product recall, it did not expect 1997 profits to be affected.
"There was a scare and you saw that reflected in the market price of the stock," Bangert's Ebbing said. "It is a fairly small incident, but they are looking slightly vulnerable."

Milupa withdrew a batch of the same product in France in February. In January it withdrew its Milumil babymilk powder from sale in Britain and Ireland because of a suggested link with Salmonella infections. The powder had been made in France. -- Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000, Fax +31 20 504 5040
